title: A Jurassic mammaliaform swimmer and transformation of the mammalian pharynx
title_zh: 侏罗纪哺乳动物形类游泳者与腭的转化
abstract: The discovery of a well-preserved mammaliaform fossil from the Middle Jurassic period of China reveals evidence on the evolutionary transformation of the feeding apparatus and the ecological diversity of Mesozoic era mammals. Mammaliaforms are evolutionary predecessors to modern Mammalia1–3, and their morphologies provide primary insights into the evolutionary origin of mammals. The rare preservation of a therian-like pharyngeal vault (throat passage) and hyoid skeletal anatomy (throat bones) in this mammaliaform suggests that critical soft-tissue anatomy for therian-like swallowing, drinking and suckling behaviours had evolved in the common ancestors of Docodonta and Mammalia, long before the rise of modern mammals. This fossil exhibits a wealth of features specialized for swimming, filling in a major gap of anatomical knowledge of pelvis and hindlimb for early mammals. It is characterized by highly distinctive canines and pseudo-carnassial sectorial teeth for a faunivorous diet. We interpret that this mammaliaform was semiaquatic, swimming and foraging in water, with a lifestyle analogous to the extant platypus. This species is the largest of Jurassic mammaliaforms. It expands the body size range of docodontans, and adds to a growing body of evidence that multiple docodontans exploited diverse niches with semiaquatic and other ecomorphotypes. Docodontans are an early example of replicated evolution of the semiaquatic and other ecomorphotypes in the Mesozoic ecosystem dominated by dinosaurs, long before the diversification of extant mammals. A swimming and water-foraging mammaliaform, Megacauda sungei gen. et sp. nov., had a lifestyle analogous to the extant platypus, and was capable of mammal-like swallowing and suckling.
abstract_zh: 来自中国中侏罗纪的完整保存哺乳动物形类化石的发现，揭示了进食器官的进化转化以及中生代哺乳动物的生态多样性。哺乳动物形类是现代哺乳动物的进化前身，其形态为哺乳动物进化的起源提供了主要见解。该哺乳动物形类稀有的有类似有兽类腭（喉道）和腭骨骨骼的保存，表明关键的软组织解剖结构——即有兽类吞咽、饮水和吸奶行为——已在双齿目和哺乳动物的共同祖先中进化，远早于现代哺乳动物的出现。该化石展示了大量适应游泳的特征，填补了早期哺乳动物骨盆和后肢的主要解剖知识空白。其特征是高度独特的尖牙和伪食肉齿列，适应食虫饮食。我们认为，该哺乳动物形类是半水生的，在水中游动和觅食，其生活方式类似于现存的鸭嘴兽。该物种是侏罗纪哺乳动物形类中体型最大的。它扩展了双齿目体型的范围，并为越来越多的证据做出了贡献，表明在恐龙主导的中生态系统中，许多双齿目利用不同的生态形态，包括半水生等，这在现代哺乳动物辐射之前就已经发生。一种游泳和水中觅食的哺乳动物形类Megacauda sungei gen. et sp. nov.，其生活方式类似于现存的鸭嘴兽，并且能够类似哺乳动物的吞咽和吸奶。
